transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to get our pre-lock round-robin started so we can move toward final production approval. We've got the gala coming up Saturday evening at the Orpheum, and I need to hear final operating requirements from each of our leads — technical, rights, talent, and accessibility. Who'd like to kick things off?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical requirement before we proceed. My completed radio-frequency survey found that wireless roaming camera links interfere with the Orpheum Theater's assistive-listening loop. Because of that, the gala must use three fixed wired cameras operating from the marked camera platforms — no wireless roaming cameras. I filed the survey in the technical folder, but I want to make sure it's reflected on Mara's draft lock sheet, since it directly affects our camera plan and the assistive-listening system.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a critical rights requirement to flag. My signed performance license — which I received countersigned this morning and haven't yet entered in the rights tracker — permits the gala broadcast but prohibits any video-on-demand release or later promotional clips. The recording must be marked broadcast-only. This directly affects our draft package, which currently permits the recording to be reused in the festival archive. That archive reuse would violate the license terms, so we need to remove that provision before lock.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a critical talent requirement to flag. I confirmed with the headliner's agent that the performer can soundcheck only at exactly 3:00 PM on Saturday, and the rider explicitly prohibits sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage. I have the agent's confirmation in email, but it is not currently reflected in the production schedule. This directly affects two things: first, the soundcheck time needs to be locked at 3:00 PM in the schedule, and second, the draft package currently includes a sponsor product display on stage, which would violate the headliner's rider.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a critical accessibility requirement to flag. My accessibility vendor confirmed that the live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B, whose dedicated return feed is connected to the gala's caption encoder. The general plan's control-room location will not work for the caption feed. I documented the vendor confirmation in the accessibility file, but I have not yet added the booth assignment to the lock sheet. This directly affects our draft package's caption feed plan — we need to lock Booth B as the captioner's operating position before final approval.

transcript.text: Thank you all for those critical flags. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my binding production approval. Devon: three fixed wired cameras only, no wireless roaming cameras, due to RF interference with the assistive-listening loop. Leila: the signed license permits broadcast only — no VOD, no promotional clips, and the festival archive reuse provision must be removed. Jonah: headliner soundcheck locked at 3:00 PM Saturday, and the sponsor product display on stage must be removed per the rider. Nia: captioner must operate from Booth B, not the general control-room location. Each of these directly conflicts with provisions in our current draft package, so I'll be updating the lock sheet to reflect all five requirements. Are there any objections before I proceed to final approval?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: No objections from me, Mara. The RF survey requirement is clear — three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms, no wireless roaming. I'll make sure my technical team is ready to operate within that constraint. One thing I want to confirm: since the camera plan is now limited to three fixed wired positions, I'd recommend we verify that the marked camera platforms still give us adequate coverage for the broadcast, given the 900-seat venue layout. But that's an operational detail I can handle on my end. You can proceed with the lock sheet update.
